title: Bureau of Street Services (StreetsLA) / City Median Conversion Program / Conversion Assessment / Resources Necessary for Phased Implementation / AB 1572 / Compliance and Potential Costs to Non-Compliance / Funding and Turf Rebate Increase
motion: I THEREFORE MOVE that the Bureau of Street Services (StreetsLA), with the assistance of the Los Angeles Department of Water and Power (LADWP), be INSTRUCTED to report in 30 days on: 1 . Existing conditions assessment and staffing needs necessary for StreetsLA to assess its approximately 10 million square feet of improved landscaped medians, identify non-functional turf, document irrigation conditions and shared tree/landscape irrigation systems, and prioritize locations for conversion; MJy, SEP 1 6 2026 2. Conversion and maintenance resources necessary for StreetsLA to establish and implement a phased Citywide median conversion program, including staffing and funding for design, construction, irrigation upgrades, plant establishment, and ongoing maintenance; and 3. An initial list of potential medians for conversion, with at least one per Council District, that details all necessary capital expenses, to pilot a City Median Conversion Program; and 4. A tailored City Median Conversion Program, developed in coordination with LADWP, to facilitate AB 1572 compliance and implementation by StreetsLA, including turf-conversion incentives, dedicated funding or financing mechanisms, and the process for receiving advanced lump sum payments and rebates for median conversion; and 5. What will happen to existing non-compliant medians should they not be converted to drought-tolerant medians, including the potential increased annual maintenance costs due to weed removal, dust mitigation, and other issues as identified by the bureau. I FURTHER MOVE that the City Administrative Officer, in coordination with the Board of Public Works, Bureau of Street Services (StreetsLA), and Department of Water and Power, be INSTRUCTED to report on potential front funding sources and grants, including but not limited to the Public Works Trust Fund, Measure M, state and federal grants, and other eligible sources. I FURTHER MOVE that the Department of Water and Power be INSTRUCTED to confer with the Metropolitan Water District and report back on the feasibility and process for increasing the rebate provided for turf conversion. 0 PRESENTED BY: IMELDA PADILLA Councilmember, 6th District
